headline: Three Democratic US senators published a report on Friday arguing that tax breaks for data centres are costing state and local governments billions of dollars.
score_reason: Pool score 7 lowered to 6: only a secondary account of the report could be read (the MLex original is paywalled) and it comes from one party's senators.
importance_line: Households and local governments weighing data centre tax breaks get an argument about who pays, but it comes from three Democratic senators and no reply from the companies is reported.
summary: Market Briefs reports that the report by Senators Elizabeth Warren, Chris Van Hollen and Richard Blumenthal says the conditions on data centre tax breaks, such as adding permanent jobs or supplying their own power, set "such a low bar that they can often be met with relative ease", leaving ratepayers, taxpayers and local communities with many of the costs. It follows TIME's exclusive of 8 Oct on the same three senators' investigation into seven large data centre developers, which we carried in our 9 Oct edition; it is not clear whether this is the same document.
notes: Follow-up of 1009:C09-04 (TIME, our 9 Oct edition item 35). MLex original https://www.mlex.com/mlex/artificial-intelligence/articles/2536509 is paywalled (headline only); text read at Market Briefs. Market Briefs gives no outlet it relies on, so it is credited as the outlet that reported it.
